method: Static reverse engineering with ILSpy, Ghidra, rizin and CLR-token inspection; no sample was executed.
external_sources: The supplied triage and MalwareBazaar pages were inaccessible through the web tool. Verdicts rely on bytes, not queue labels or scores.

samples.identification: Self-named NanoCoreUltimate .NET surveillance and disruption program; canonical NanoCore family attribution is not established.
evidence: Main directly blocks input, disables security services, poisons security-vendor hosts entries and invokes fodhelper registry hijacking before starting surveillance tasks.
StartKeylogger installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL and also polls GetAsyncKeyState. Both append key records and FlushKeylog passes them to the local logging routine.

AccessWindowsCredentialManager enumerates LocalApplicationData/Microsoft/Credentials and copies files into its staging directory. Browser login databases, wallet files, clipboard data and screenshots are also collected.

InstallPersistence writes its assembly location to Run keys, copies into Startup and creates logon and recurring tasks. USBWorm copies itself as a hidden executable and writes an AutoRun open directive.

ActivateBotnetWhenPdfOpened replaces the PDF class and open command with this executable. CreateFakeDecryptor copies the same program as a decryptor; CreateBackdoorAccount invokes user creation and administrator-group addition.
limits: IsPlaceholder always returns true; ParseC2Url clears the domain. SendToC2 logs locally before returning, so the apparent HTTP/DNS exfiltration is disabled.
AES_KEY is 16 bytes and AES_IV is 14 bytes. Setting the IV throws before encryption can write replacement files or delete originals. RealEncryption targets Desktop/TestFolder only.
Injection uses RET-only test bytes; DumpLSASS opens a process handle but does not dump its memory.

The program uses simulation wording, but has no required consent/configuration guard before global disruption, persistence, credential staging and deceptive self-copy behavior. No authorized testing context was supplied.

samples.identification: StormAttack resource-DLL installer, configured for the Active Setup branch.
evidence: At 0x401cb0 the mode byte at 0x404120 is 3, selecting Active Setup self-copy and cleanup code.
0x401900 creates a GUID-named Active Setup component, writes its copied executable path to StubPath, reads and patches its own image and launches the copy.
0x401150 starts an IE/notepad/calc target, allocates remote memory, writes the DLL path, resolves LoadLibraryA and passes the remote buffer to CreateRemoteThread.
0x401260 deletes and replaces LanmanServer Parameters/ServiceDLL. 0x401390 builds COMSPEC /c del using the current short module path.
Resource DLL/101 is extracted through 0x402460 and written through 0x4023c0. Banners, service names and the dropped DLL name corroborate StormAttack identity.
limits: The embedded PE is approximately 94.49% zero bytes. Its entry point (RVA 0x741a), resources, relocations and import data are zeroed. No working DDoS payload or successful DLL load is established.
Some calls and self-patching offsets are damaged; installation may fail. The surviving injection, persistence and cleanup code establishes hostile purpose despite those defects.
No legitimate deployment or product context was supplied. Filename references to other malware families are not evidence of those families.

samples.identification: Ghost Telegram remote-command agent, native MinGW PE, build G7CDD6836.
evidence: 0x140003290 implements RC4 KSA and PRGA. Offline decryption of immediate-built buffers recovers api.telegram.org, bot getUpdates routes, registration JSON and persistence/notification commands. Bot credentials are deliberately omitted from this record.

0x140005670 initializes baked-in bot/chat configuration, registers host identity, polls updates with jitter, selects the configured chat, Base64-decodes and authenticates/decrypts tasks, parses task fields and dispatches by command hash.

Dispatch reaches pipe-backed process execution, file access/upload/download, process termination and domain reconnaissance. Responses and files are encrypted with AES-256-CBC plus HMAC-SHA256 and returned via Telegram.

0x140005500 starts both a local NTLM listener (0x140003a40) and an SSPI client (0x1400015c0). The listener supplies a challenge, parses the NTLM type-3 response and formats the captured NetNTLMv2 credentials for return.

Persistence commands use a security-tray-like Run value and suppress StartupApp/NewAppInstalled notifications. 0x140001c80 passes SECURITY_FLAGS 31 with certificate-ignore bits 0x3300 to WinHttpSetOption.
limits: The UAC-bypass wording belongs to an elevation-status report; no UAC bypass implementation was established.

The supplied ransomware labels are not supported by victim-file encryption code. Crypto protects C2 messages; the file decrypt command applies a supplied XOR key, writes an executable and removes the encrypted input.

The unsigned GUI binary has fixed operator configuration, stealth/persistence controls and credential capture. Those facts tip the verdict toward an implant; no authorized remote-administration context was supplied. Corpus provenance alone did not decide the verdict.

trait_changes: Bind LocalApplicationData/Microsoft/Credentials ldstr arguments to their CLR #US entries; fix the missed directory-copy finding without requiring heap adjacency.
Add a key-independent RC4 PRGA compiler variant and an IAT-bound x64 WinHTTP certificate-ignore setup detection, both notable.
Remove arbitrary UAC-bypass wording as a bypass predicate; retain mechanism-specific predicates.

Move the firing Winsock/HTTP observation into micro-behaviors, require both JSON and connection-close headers, and update its two explicit C2 consumers. Deliberately stop inheriting unrelated endpoint/UA alternatives in this neutral header observation.
verification: All three targets rescanned with atomscan. Fifteen static positive/near-miss controls passed, including inert PE status/HTTP controls; final repository validation is run after judgement markers.
